conventions.decoded: present only when expect is ok; type is the numeric frame type, payload_hex the payload bytes in lowercase hex
conventions.expect: ok: the frame passes every stateless check of preview tunnel v1 T2; close_1002: the receiver closes the tunnel with close code 1002
conventions.fill: optional fill_byte (one lowercase hex byte) and fill_count: the message is hex followed by fill_byte repeated fill_count times; decoded.payload_fill_byte and decoded.payload_fill_count apply the same rule to payload_hex; fill is used only when the repeated run is over 1024 bytes
conventions.frames: stateless decoding only; stream ordering, windows and limits are covered by sequences
conventions.hex: one complete websocket binary message, lowercase hex: 1 byte type, 4 bytes big-endian stream id, then the payload
conventions.length: required: the total message length in bytes after fill expansion; replayers must assert it
conventions.open: present for OPEN: the strictly parsed preview_id and preview_key
conventions.receiver: frames are judged as received by the runner; a gateway receiving OPEN closes 1002 regardless of payload
conventions.reset_code: present for RESET: the code name the receiver acts on; an unknown code decodes ok and maps to protocol
conventions.sequence_expect: ok: the runner accepts the message and the tunnel stays open; drop: the message names an odd stream id at or below the highest opened id that is not open (closed, reset, or skipped by the gateway), it is ignored without any reply or state change; close_1002: the runner closes the tunnel with close code 1002 and sends nothing more; close_1002 is always the last step; a second END is drop once both ENDs have closed the stream and close_1002 while the stream is still open
conventions.sequence_replies: replies_hex is the complete, ordered list of messages the runner sends because of that step, including replies that depend on the upstream such as RESET after a failed lookup, END after the upstream closes, or WINDOW after bytes reach the upstream; the runner sends nothing else; a replayer waits for exactly these replies, then waits for 50 ms of silence before delivering the next step; the 50 ms is advisory for replay only and is not a protocol timing rule; when a sequence ends without close_1002 the gateway closes the tunnel
conventions.sequence_step: from is always gateway: hex, expanded with fill_byte and fill_count exactly as for frames and checked against length, is one websocket binary message the runner receives
conventions.sequence_upstream: upstream is how the local upstream behind every known preview behaves: discard reads and discards all bytes and never writes or closes, ignoring the runner's half-close; close_on_eof reads and discards and closes its side once it reads EOF, so the runner sends END; stall accepts the connection and never reads, writes or closes, so gateway DATA stays queued and unconsumed
conventions.sequences: stateful replays from the runner's point of view; each sequence starts on a fresh tunnel; known_previews are the hosted previews the runner owns, all deployed and unexpired; an OPEN naming any other preview_id, or a known preview_id with a different preview_key, is answered with RESET not_found and nothing is dialed; steps run in order
conventions.stream_id_rule: every frame needs an odd, non-zero stream id; even ids are a protocol error in both directions
conventions.upstream_checks: optional per step: upstream_receives_hex is the complete byte string, in lowercase hex, that the upstream of the step's stream id must have received from the runner since that stream was opened, by the end of the step (an empty string means nothing); upstream_eof true means that upstream has read the runner's half-close by then, false means it has not; each is absent when not asserted, and neither appears in stall sequences
conventions.window_credit: present for WINDOW: the uint32 big-endian credit
conventions.window_policy: runner policy, not protocol: credit is granted only after bytes are written to the upstream, as one WINDOW per stream once at least 131072 written bytes are ungranted, never while 16777216 or more received bytes are unconsumed across the tunnel, and withheld credit is sent once the total drops below that; a gateway must not rely on grant size or timing beyond the spec
